title: design: prototype v2 of the living ship, at a designer's standard
acceptance: The captain found the board's ship does not match the approved prototype (hull, crew actions, props, handoffs) and wants more than parity: a ship that sails a living sea, at a designer's standard rather than engineering CSS and SVG pieced together. Settled with the captain on 2026-09-24: parity with prototype v1 element by element; the ship centred, riding the swell, with parallax, bow spray and a wake; motion tied to real state; animation only when state changes outside the sea's idle swell; idle CPU below 10% of one core, animations paused in a hidden tab, and a static scene under prefers-reduced-motion plus a motion switch; layered SVG for sea, sky and hull with a small spring and easing engine; DOM figures kept for drag and click. This task is design only: a prototype v2 the captain approves before T-060 to T-064 and the motion task build it. Its own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

Load and follow the frontend-design skill (installed as the frontend-design plugin) for this work. Design plan (firstmate, following the frontend-design skill's first pass; the worker builds against it and may refine it with stated reasons). SUBJECT: a captain's board commanding a crew of AI agents; the ship is a living diorama of the crew's real work. AUDIENCE: one engineer-captain who glances at it many times a day. PRIMARY JOB: at a glance, who is working, what is blocked, and what waits for the captain. DIRECTION (captain-settled, D in chat 2026-09-24): a refined tilt-shift ship-model diorama that evolves the prototype's blocky figures, not a new cast. Materials, not accents: Stockholm tar #3A2418 (hull), sailcloth #E8DDC4 (sails, tags), binnacle brass #C99A3C (fittings, rails, lettering), ensign red #B23A2E (main course, rejection), sea-glass #6FA8A0 (approval, calm water highlights), Prussian ink #0E2A3B (deep water at night). The sky follows the captain's local time with four keyed palettes (dawn rose #E7A58C into pearl, day #8FC1D4, dusk #D9774A into violet #5B4A7A, night #0A1A2A with moon), and state weather layers over it: calm (no work in flight), breeze (work in flight, wind and speed scale with the number of live runs), squall (a red gate or a card waiting on the captain: darker cloud band, higher swell, spray), clearing (a merge: light breaks, salvo, bell). TYPE: one display face used in one place, the ship's name plate and rate, cut like an engraved chart (IM Fell English SC, OFL, vendored as woff2 under the proposal folder); everything else one condensed humanist sans for tags and labels (Barlow Semi Condensed, OFL, vendored). Sentence case; no all-caps labels; no monospace data labels. LAYOUT: the sea is a wide band; the ship sits centred and never drifts off its anchor point; parallax bands behind it (far islands, clouds, horizon glow) and in front (near swell, foam) move at different speeds to make forward travel; bow spray and a wake trail the hull. Name tags float above the crew as sailcloth pennants, not UI cards. PRINCIPLES: the one bold thing is the ship on a living sea; the rest of the board stays quiet. Every motion encodes state: nothing moves for decoration alone except the sea's idle swell. Light is the diorama's signature: one key light from the sun or moon position of the local time, a rim light on figures, soft contact shadows on deck, gentle depth-of-field blur on the nearest and farthest planes. Self-check against generated-design defaults: the palette is material- and time-driven, never 'dark background plus one bright accent'; no cream-and-terracotta; no identical rounded cards; brass is a material on fittings, not a highlight colour for text.

Captain, 2026-09-24, after seeing round one ('prototype v2 沒有把現有的卡片管理等等整個網頁都渲染出來', then '需要補足'): prototype v2 is the whole captain's board page, as v1 was, not the ship scene alone. With fake data and working interactions, it renders everything the live board has today: - the header with its counts (merged, in flight, waiting on you, blocked, ready, backlog); - the lanes backlog, ready, working, gate, review, captain and merged, with lane cards, their #n pull-request links and their menus; - park and drop by drag and by the menu, with the in-page drop confirmation and the collapsed parked group; - the decision deck, with a choice card (A/B/C/D and custom) and a merge card, each with its authored diagram frame; - the crew roster and the live event log; - the ship scene as approved. The whole page takes the ship's visual language (the material palette, Barlow Semi Condensed and IM Fell English SC) without losing information density or readability. Secondary text stays at least 13px and primary at least 16px, and lanes and cards read as a ship's log and chart table, not generic SaaS cards. The page is alive only where state changes (Q4): a card slides to its new lane, a new card fades in, counts roll to their new value, and a merge plays the salvo across the ship. Switches demonstrate each of these. The approved ship scene is kept as it is.

Captain feedback, 2026-09-24: every worker's and reviewer's pennant, and its roster row, shows the vendor and model the run uses (for example 'claude · opus-5'), with fake data in the prototype. T-085 does the real plumbing.
Captain decision D-1024 = A: at most 3 masts. 1 mast for 1–3 crew, 2 for 4–8, 3 from 9 up; decks, length and guns still grow with the crew. The prototype's rate switch follows this.

Deliver design/proposals/2026-09-24-ship-v2/prototype.html: self-contained, opens from disk with no network, and uses only vendored fonts and inline assets. It has keyboard or on-screen switches to show every state the captain must judge: the four times of day; the four weathers; rates 1 to 6 per D-1009 (cutter to man-o'-war, 1 to 6 masts); crew counts from 1 to 24; each crew action; the captain's idle, ready and order poses; a handoff of each kind (order, pull request, approval, rejection) passing between figures; a merge salvo with bell; an order with bell and whistle (D-1010); and reduced motion.

Every prototype v1 element is present and at least as refined: perspective elliptical decks with planks, riser walls, capped bulwarks and one hull volume; the figurehead and trailboard; mast placement from the top deck with exactly one main mast carrying the red course, skull and Jolly Roger; the captain's full outfit and two-arm poses; deck-pooled crew actions with left-hand tools and deck props; per-kind handoff arcs; smoke with the salvo. Nothing v1 or design.md excludes returns: no percentages, no random progress, no simulated dispatch, secondary text at least 13px and primary at least 16px, and one captain on the top deck.

Deliver design/proposals/2026-09-24-ship-v2/motion-spec.md: for every moving thing, its period, amplitude, easing curve (named or cubic-bezier), trigger (idle or which state change), what it encodes, and its reduced-motion replacement; the per-weather parameters; and the CPU budget with how it is measured. Also a README.md there listing the switches and the design decisions with their reasons, including anything the worker changed from firstmate's plan and why.

Evidence: the required GitHub check and the seven gates. The worker cannot run or screenshot anything. Firstmate renders the prototype in a browser after each round, posts screenshots and critique on the pull request, and the captain approves the look on a choice card before T-060 to T-064 build it.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
